blocks.text: **The task.** Reverse only the vowels of a string, leaving every other character exactly where it is.
This is the reversal problem with a filter on top. The vowels, read in order, must come out reversed — but the consonants must not move at all.
You could collect the vowels, reverse that list, and write them back. That works and costs O(N) space. Two pointers does it in one pass with none.
Walk from both ends, but only stop when a pointer is sitting on a vowel. When both are, swap them and step inward. Consonants are simply skipped over.
Why a Set for the vowels

`vowels.has(ch)` is O(1). A string search like `'aeiou'.includes(ch)` scans up to five characters each time — still constant, but a Set states the intent more clearly and does not grow if you later add more characters.

This is the palindrome solution with two edits: the skip condition tests for vowels instead of punctuation, and the body swaps instead of compares. Recognising that shared skeleton is what makes the pattern valuable — you are not learning problems, you are learning one loop.
**Space: O(N)** for the character array, only because JavaScript strings are immutable. In a language with mutable strings this is O(1).
